content: Persian tobacco, also known as Tanbaku, flowering tobacco, ornamental tobacco, or winged tobacco, is scientifically referred to as Nicotiana alata. This specific type of tobacco originates from Iran and is exclusively used in narghilas (water pipes). Unlike conventional tobacco, Persian tobacco is not chopped but is instead broken apart manually by hand. Another species of tobacco, Nicotiana persica, is cultivated in Persia (modern-day Iran) and serves as the source of Persian tobacco. This type of tobacco is produced under the ITC monopoly. The term Persian tobacco is also referenced in literature, such as in Mark Twain's book Innocents Abroad, specifically in Chapter XXXIV.
